decisions.text: The squad's fines kitty has £100k in it from late arrivals and phones in meetings. The head coach asks where it should go. The local paper always runs it when it goes to charity.

options.label: Give it to the club's community partner (press mood +2)
Put it in the transfer pot (£100k into the transfer budget)
Leave it in the kitty (nothing changes)

decisions.text: A sponsor wants the squad at a photo shoot on the day off and will pay £200k for the afternoon. The supporters trust has asked for the same afternoon for an open day at the training ground, and the local paper wants to cover it.
decisions.resolved: Nobody answered before the next match, so nothing changed.

decisions.text: Board patience was 6 when this note was written. They want a progress review; the press officer offers an update too.
decisions.resolved: Nobody answered before the next match, so nothing changed.

decisions.text: The head coach flags Myles Lewis-Skelly: his morale is down at 49, the lowest in the first team squad, and a word from the manager would help.
decisions.resolved: Nobody answered before the next match, so nothing changed.

decisions.text: A local school has asked for a first team visit, and the community department would like the manager to front it. The board like to see the manager doing this sort of thing.
decisions.resolved: Nobody answered before the next match, so nothing changed.

decisions.text: Cristhian Mosquera was shown a straight red against Newcastle and is banned for 1 match. The club secretary rates an appeal at 40 percent. Win and the ban is wiped. Lose and the panel makes it 2 matches. It has to go in before the next match.
decisions.resolved: No appeal went in before the next match, so the 1 match ban stood.
